title: Need air conditioning? Consider the heat pump.
summary: A 2025 Canary Media guide arguing that anyone replacing central AC should consider a heat pump, with costs, savings and incentives.

assertions.quote: All-electric heat pumps are ACs, but better.
it costs between $900 and $1,900 more to replace a broken central AC with a heat pump instead of a conventional AC
installing a heat pump in a single-family home in the region typically costs $1,000 less than installing a gas furnace and AC

verdicts.note: In cold-climate ducted homes with central AC the minimum-efficiency heat pump averages $2,000 less than furnace plus AC, but medium and high-efficiency units cost $8,000 and $13,000 more.
Edwards' median installed heat pump ($6,185) costs about $270 less than a gas furnace plus central AC and about $90 more than resistance plus AC, with over 80% of the cost distributions overlapping.
RMI says customers replacing both an AC and a furnace can save installation cost by choosing one heat pump for both jobs.

LBNL archetypes: electric equipment (ductless heat pump plus heat pump water heater, $14,754) cost more than gas ($8,786), but the gap almost exactly equals the $5,930 cost of adding central air, implying no premium when comparing heating plus cooling like for like.
When both furnace and AC need replacing, a ccASHP with propane furnace backup costs only $370 more than a new furnace plus AC (payback under about one year).
Compared with the gas-plus-AC baseline, the Canadian model finds heat pumps have higher upfront costs and win only on lifetime costs through efficiency and doubling as cooling.

assertions.quote: For most households, these two-in-one appliances pay for themselves in reduced energy bills over their estimated 16-year lifetime.

verdicts.note: Picking the best package per home, 59% (65 million) have positive unsubsidized NPV over 16 years, but no single package exceeds 55%, and that is an idealized best choice.
With minimum-efficiency heat pumps, 7% discount rate and 15-year life, only 21% of US single-family houses would gain economically.

Edwards cites earlier studies finding only about 30% of households would benefit from a single-speed heat pump and newer cold-climate studies about 60%; its own bill model gives 53% with 28% uncertain, so the majority is thin and depends on assumptions.
RMI concludes that most of the 56 million gas-heated US households would not find a heat pump cost-effective at 2018 prices, although propane, oil and new-build homes would.
Modelling of five Canadian cities finds a heat pump is the lowest lifetime-cost heating and cooling option for most households; this is Canada with its rebates and carbon price, not the US.

assertions.quote: Families that go from relying on expensive delivered fuels to electric heat pumps unlock the biggest cost savings
Households ditching gas heating can see an average of $60 in savings per year.
Utility customers with access to electricity rates that favor heat pumps can save even more.
the Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit, which can take up to $2,000 off your federal tax bill for a qualifying heat pump
While some state programs have rolled out after being finalized under the Biden administration, others still awaiting approvals are now stuck in limbo.
